MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
REFERRING CLINICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]
DATE OF REPORT: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Fragile-X syndrome

METHODOLOGY
PCR assay for FRAXA expansion mutation detection in FMR1 gene

DNA was extracted from peripheral blood. PCR amplification of the CGG repeat region in the FMR1 gene was performed using fluorescent primers flanking the repeat region. Fragment analysis was carried out by capillary electrophoresis. This method reliably detects normal and premutation alleles up to approximately 200 CGG repeats.

RESULTS
Gene: FMR1 (OMIM *309550)
Allele size: 35 (±1) CGG repeats
Interpretation: NORMAL

Reference ranges (ACGS Guidelines 2014):
- Normal: 6-45 CGG repeats
- Intermediate: 46-54 CGG repeats
- Premutation: 55-200 CGG repeats
- Full mutation: >200 CGG repeats

SUMMARY
Normal allele with 35 (±1) CGG repeats detected. Within normal range (6-45 repeats) per ACGS Guidelines (2014).

The patient is very unlikely to be affected with Fragile-X syndrome based on this result.

TEST LIMITATIONS
This PCR-based method detects CGG repeat expansions in the FMR1 gene. A small proportion (<1%) of Fragile-X syndrome cases may be caused by point mutations or rearrangements not detected by this method. If clinical suspicion remains high, please contact the laboratory to discuss further testing options.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorised by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Scientist
